historical_claims.anchor: Maxwell's distribution gives a precise prediction of the spread of speeds for a classical gas at equilibrium.
For a classical, dilute gas made from individual atoms, each atom has three independent components of translational motion.
historical_claims.source_locator: Equipartition and monatomic gas degrees of freedom

historical_claims.anchor: For a mole of ideal gas at fixed temperature, a reversible expansion to twice its starting volume has an entropy change equal to the gas constant times the natural logarithm of two.
The hot reservoir loses entropy: one hundred joules divided by four hundred kelvin, or a quarter of a joule per kelvin.

The ideal reversible engine operating between reservoirs at a hot temperature and a cold temperature has a maximum efficiency equal to one minus the cold absolute temperature divided by the hot absolute temperature.
For a reversible pump the coefficient of performance for heating, defined as heat delivered indoors divided by work supplied, is three hundred divided by thirty, or ten.
historical_claims.source_locator: Reversible heat pump coefficient of performance

historical_claims.anchor: At constant temperature and pressure, a useful potential is the Gibbs free energy: enthalpy minus temperature times entropy.

In particular, resetting a bit of memory that has equally probable logical states has a minimum heat cost of Boltzmann's constant times temperature times the natural logarithm of two in the standard ideal isothermal erasure limit.

description: Develops the thermodynamics of heat engines from microscopic molecular motion, energy conservation, entropy, Carnot efficiency, and the need for a cold reservoir, then connects the same limits to heat pumps, free energy, and information erasure.
